native.previewPolicy: HTML/CSS entries are schematic documentation previews using browser system colors and typography. They do not reproduce AppKit colors, SwiftUI text metrics, SF Symbols, interaction behavior, or discovered device data. Native source mappings are authoritative.

evidenceScope.basis: Final SwiftUI source, successful Swift build and 11 passing tests; native layout behavior was observed before the final compact-caption and selected-foreground changes. The independent source review found no material defect; the formal visual finish review awaits recapture because native automation failed globally.
observed: Real discovered disk hierarchy, native disclosure and row selection.
Inspector popover in a narrow workspace.
evidenceScope.noClaim: This documentation does not certify the full application surface.

sourceRelationships.relationship: Owns DiskStore and the NavigationSplitView shell; embeds DeviceSidebar and DeviceWorkspaceView with WorkspaceLayout constraints.
Uses the inventory node hierarchy in a selectable List and OutlineGroup; owns bounded row presentation and contextual commands.
Owns toolbar commands, operation/discovery states, DeviceDetailView and inline/popover DeviceInspector presentation.
Defines the window and pane budget plus the inline-inspector width condition.
Shares real DeviceActionButtons between the toolbar Actions menu and DeviceContextMenu; also defines NoticeView.

components.name: Physical Partition Map
components.description: Physical-byte-scaled partition track with a linked adaptive text legend; empty schematic preview avoids fabricated partitions.
components.html:
Partition Map
Segment widths show physical partition capacity.
components.css: .ds-partition-map { color-scheme: light dark; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; font-family: system-ui; color: CanvasText; } .ds-partition-track { height: 38px; border-radius: 5px; background: ButtonFace; overflow: hidden; } .ds-partition-note { color: GrayText; }
components.nativeSource: PartitionMapLayout(disk: disk) supplies segments to GeometryReader. Track buttons use segment.lengthFraction and segment.startFraction, select(segment.id), system hues by segment.index, opacity 1 or 0.75, and a 2-point primary stroke on selection. LazyVGrid with adaptive minimum 240 supplies a matching button for every segment. The 38-point track clips to RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5).
components.nativeGeometry: PartitionMapLayout accepts a positive physical-disk capacity. Segment start uses the reported offset or prior partition end; missing length preserves that start, and overflow saturates the next end. Start and length fractions clamp to physical-disk bounds. The legend uses 8-point circles and the same system hue as its segment, names up to two lines, identifiers and tabular capacities. It supplies a full-size text target even for tiny physical segments.

narrative.overview:
Diskvio uses familiar macOS controls to make storage relationships legible. Its identity comes from clear hierarchy, real metadata, consistent spacing, and restrained emphasis. System typography, SF Symbols, and native selection and focus treatments keep the interface at home on macOS.

The application is a working utility with concise labels, readable properties, and enough separation to distinguish devices, capacity summaries, and supporting explanations. Light and dark appearance follow platform semantics. This document records the implemented SwiftUI system; it does not certify untested runtime states.
keyCharacteristics: Native SwiftUI navigation, lists, forms, toolbars, and context menus.
Semantic text hierarchy and appearance-aware platform colors.
Flat surfaces with structural dividers and restrained tonal emphasis.
SF Symbols and text labels that explain storage relationships.
Resizable panes and scrollable detail content.

rules.name: The Platform Appearance Rule
rules.body: Use the existing semantic platform colors and native control states so appearance follows macOS.

rules.name: The Metadata Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Keep names and values primary, and use secondary captions for their labels and context.

rules.name: The Content Width Rule
rules.body: Preserve the central workspace's minimum width and move properties to the inspector popover when the inline pane budget does not fit.

rules.name: The Physical Scale Rule
rules.body: Map geometry follows real physical partition bytes and offsets; container and volume sharing remain explicit in text.

dos: Do use native macOS SwiftUI controls, SF Symbols, system typography, and semantic colors.
Do preserve primary values with secondary labels and the implemented spacing roles.
Do use tabular digits for capacity values and retain explicit shared-capacity language for APFS volumes.
Do pair partition hues with names, identifiers, and capacities.
Do retain resizable panes, scrollable detail, the inspector toggle, and explicit unavailable metadata.
donts: Don't replace appearance-aware native colors or semantic text styles with guessed fixed values.
Don't assign status or filesystem meaning to the partition color sequence.
Don't render shared APFS volume capacity as an independent physical partition.
Don't generalize the map radius into a custom style for native controls.
Don't present source-level layout or accessibility affordances as runtime validation.
